Chronology 1 — Creation

Part III walks the shared storyline from creation to the end. At each stage: the Bible's text, the Qur'an's text, where they converge, where they collide, then a present/weigh/judge verdict. The recurring finding will be that one continuous theological seam — God's nature → sin → forgiveness → Christ → the end — runs through every episode.

The Bible's text

  • Genesis 1: creation in six days, ordered — light (1); sky/ firmament (2); land, sea, plants (3); sun, moon, stars (4); fish, birds (5); land animals and humankind, male and female (6); God rests (7), hallowing the Sabbath (Gen 2:2–3).
  • Genesis 2: a second, differently-ordered account — the man formed first from dust, then the garden, then animals, then woman from his side.
  • Creation is by divine speech ("And God said… and it was so"); the NT reads this as creation from nothing (Heb 11:3; John 1:3; Col 1:16).

The Qur'an's text

  • Creation in six "days" (ayyam, periods): Q 7:54; 10:3; 25:59.
  • By sheer command: "Be — and it is" (kun fayakun, Q 2:117; 36:82).
  • Heavens and earth were a joined mass, then parted (Q 21:30); the heaven "expanded" (Q 51:47).
  • Humankind from clay / dust / a drop (Q 15:26; 22:5; 32:7–9); Adam taught "the names" (Q 2:31); the angels prostrate to Adam, Iblis refuses (Q 2:34).
  • A breakdown in Q 41:9–12 lists earth in 2 + sustenance in 4 + heavens in 2 — read additively this looks like eight, the classic 6-vs-8 exegetical crux (resolved by traditional exegetes as overlapping, not additive, periods).

Convergence

Six creative periods; a single God creating by fiat, with no rival deity and no pre-existent co-creator; humankind formed from earth/ clay; a primordial couple; a tempter figure.

Collision

  1. Internal Genesis tension: Gen 1 (plants day 3, before the sun day 4; humans last) vs. Gen 2 (man before plants and animals) — a well-known source-critical seam in the Bible itself.
  2. The Qur'an's 6-vs-8 arithmetic of Q 41:9–12 — an internal exegetical knot, paralleling Genesis's internal knot.
  3. Does God rest? Gen 2:2–3 has God resting on the seventh day. Q 50:38 states creation occurred "and no fatigue touched Us" — which reads naturally as a deliberate correction of Genesis. This is a genuine theological divergence, not a copying detail: it flows straight from the nature-of-God contrast (absolute transcendence vs. an anthropomorphic-friendly text).

Arbiter verdict — creation

Present. Both: one God, six periods, creation by command, man from earth. Bible adds Sabbath rest and a two-account structure; Qur'an adds "join-then-part" and the kun fayakun formula.

Weigh.

  • Symmetric weakness: each text carries an internal ordering/number puzzle (Genesis's two accounts; the Qur'an's 6-vs-8). Neither can use it against the other without conceding its own (Methodology §3).
  • Real divergence: the "God rests" vs. "no fatigue" point is substantive and textual, and Q 50:38 looks corrective by design.
  • Out of remit: concordance with modern cosmology/biology is argued apologetically on both sides; the arbiter does not rule on science- vs-text harmonization (Methodology §5).

Judge. On the shared frame: a draw — strikingly similar. On the internal puzzles: a draw — both have one. On "does God rest": a clean divergence, with the Qur'an's wording functioning as an explicit revision of Genesis; which portrayal is "better" depends on the prior theology-of-God premise already shown to be non-arbitrable (cap. 09). The seam appears immediately.
